summary: An abandoned fire lookout still stands on Goat Peak near Beaverdell, reached by forest service roads and a walk; the sources give no build date.

access.note: Reached by forest service road and a walk. A 4x4 can drive the Boyer FSR to the base; parts of the road are deactivated. No closure or permission rule was found in the sources.

visit.trail_note: A July 2026 trip report logged 11.3 km total distance and 399 m of climbing; its round-trip time includes a vehicle ride down part of the road.

notes_for_editor: No build, staffing or fire date in the pages read. A search snippet from a BC Forest Fire Lookouts Facebook group comment cites BC Forest Service annual reports for a 1913 station and cabin; the page was login-walled and the comment could not be read, so it is not used. Record kind 'tower' fits the 2026 visit, which describes going inside the lookout. Access advice differs: Life is Adventure (2021) says a 4x4 can drive to the base, and other visitors may walk about 5 km; the July 2026 trip describes a walk from road's end, so check current road conditions. Record location (49.41409, -119.01528) not checked against the OSM way.
